bytes.c prints 42 00 00 00 from index 0 up. The claim puts that layout down to 'this machine', which is little-endian with a 4-byte int, and the 6.2.6.1 p2/p4 passages support the object representation via memcpy and the implementation-defined byte order.

It also gives an implementation-defined size and byte layout (8 bytes, 00 ... 80 50 40) without 'on this machine'.
